content.title: About
content.content: The "Chocolate Wafer" cookie is a crisp wafer roll coated with a layer of milk chocolate. It is made from wheat flour, sugar, vegetable fats and cocoa butter, offering a sweet, slightly bitter flavor and a light texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wafer cookies first appeared in Europe in the 19th century as a light tea snack.
The chocolate coating usually covers only one side of the wafer, creating a contrast between crunchy texture and smooth glaze.
Caramelization of sugar in the dough gives the characteristic golden color.
The cookie is often sold in single‑serve packages, convenient for on‑the‑go snacking.
In some countries the "Chocolate Wafer" is a traditional holiday gift.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Contains fast‑acting carbohydrates that quickly raise blood glucose, providing immediate energy.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa butter in the chocolate coating is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Provides small amounts of iron that support normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough supplies modest amounts of B1, B2 and niacin, involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Satiety satisfaction
items.content: Sweet taste and crunchy texture promote a feeling of fullness and may reduce overeating.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Some versions are coated with vegetable fats containing trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain gluten, soy lecithin and milk chocolate—potential allergens.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The cookie is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a standalone snack, paired with coffee or tea, or incorporate it into desserts—crumble into ice cream, yogurt or baked goods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a dry, cool place in an airtight package. For longer shelf life keep refrigerated to prevent the chocolate coating from melting.
